articles.headline: How to bet Steelers Browns on TNF: Analysis, tips and top prop plays
articles.description: Odds, bets and analysis to help you bet Steelers-Browns on "Thursday Night Football."
articles.body:
The surprising 2-1 Cleveland Browns host the (maybe not so surprising, but still notable) 2-1 Pittsburgh Steelers on "Thursday Night Football" in a matchup I broke down in depth in my column earlier this week. I love the Steelers' ability to get to heavy personnel and run a variety of concepts, and perennially underrated back Jaylen Warren is seeing the field well behind his retooled offensive line. New starting right guard Brock Hoffman and rookie right tackle Max Iheanachor give the Steelers a five-across that can hang with anyone.

But the Browns have a fast and aggressive front featuring second-year defensive tackle Mason Graham, free-agent linebacker Quincy Williams and trade acquisition Jared Verse. Cleveland's offense has been nothing special, but the defense can create short fields and keep games close. Against an immobile quarterback like Aaron Rodgers, the pass rush has a chance to really shine.

Significant injuries in this game include cornerback Jalen Ramsey, who may try to go despite a broken wrist. His absence would dramatically impact the Steelers' pass rush and run defense approach, as they've been playing Ramsey in the box as part of their disguised looks. Browns center Elgton Jenkins looks unlikely to go, which is a particularly big deal against a Steelers defensive tackle room loaded with waves of talent (Cameron Heyward, Keeanu Benton, Derrick Harmon and Yahya Black). Starting guard Teven Jenkins did not practice Monday but was limited Tuesday, which is a good sign for his availability. The status of Joey Porter Jr., the Steelers' star corner in need of a new contract, is as always uncertain.

Betting outlook

The Steelers offense had a peak day against the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 3, but they still bring into this contest a bottom-10 offense by success rate (29th), EPA per play (30th) and points per drive (29th). The Cleveland offense has been a little better, but the Browns have played easier defenses and remain bottom 10 in all three metrics. It is hard to trust either unit to move the football consistently, though both defenses have been liable to surrendering explosive plays. This does not feel like a night to take player prop overs, but some longest reception or rush props may be in play as one-offs.

The Steelers are 2.5-point road favorites with heavy juice, which is appropriate given their advantages in the offensive trenches and at quarterback. If this is, as expected, a low-scoring game (total of 38.5), it's fair to side with the Steelers to grind out more positive runs and with Rodgers to avoid the backbreaking turnover that may swing this one.

The pick: UNDER 38.5 total points (-115)

Without turnovers and short fields, it's hard to see many touchdown drives in this game. Neither offense is consistent enough down-to-down to turn red zone appearances into seven points, and they'll have to rely on explosives to hit paydirt. I also expect a fast clock, with the Steelers leaning on their running game against a pen

articles.headline: Fantasy basketball: Players to know and position battles to watch during NBA preseason
articles.description: Eric Moody points out which preseason NBA position battles could have big fantasy ramifications.
articles.body:
As the NBA gears up for an exciting training camp and preseason, fantasy basketball managers should keep a close eye on key position battles across the league.

Who wins and loses these competitions for starting spots and more minutes will go a long way toward shaping players' fantasy value. Unlike the NFL, where position battles often revolve around executing specific plays or packages, basketball's fight for playing time is far more nuanced. Success on the hardwood depends not just on individual skill but also on chemistry and fit with teammates.

After a busy offseason of roster changes and player movement, these looming position battles add an extra layer of intrigue as fantasy basketball draft season begins.

Portland Trail Blazers backcourt: Damian Lillard, Ja Morant, Jrue Holiday, Scoot Henderson, Deni Avdija

Portland has a lot to sort out in the backcourt with Shaedon Sharpe (meniscus) sidelined for the next five months. Lillard and Morant should command major roles, but Holiday and Henderson also need minutes. Avdija adds another layer after averaging 24.2 points, 6.9 rebounds and 6.7 assists last season with much of the offense running through him.

What to watch for: How often Lillard and Morant's minutes are staggered, whether Avdija continues to initiate offense and if Henderson controls the second unit. If Henderson consistently gets 25-plus minutes with meaningful time on the ball, he moves into the late-round conversation.

New Orleans Pelicans center: Derik Queen, Yves Missi

Queen and Missi give New Orleans two very different options at center. Queen brings more scoring and playmaking, while Missi offers rebounding, rim protection and athleticism. Queen averaged 5.3 assists per 36 minutes as a rookie, which gives New Orleans a level of creation at center that Missi doesn't provide.

What to watch for: Which big man gets the majority of the center minutes, who spends more time with the starters and who closes games. If Queen handles the larger role, his all-around offensive game gives him the stronger fantasy ceiling. If the split stays close, Missi can still help managers looking for rebounds and blocks.

Houston Rockets backcourt: Reed Sheppard, Fred VanVleet, Marcus Smart

Houston has another crowded backcourt with VanVleet returning and the defensive-minded Smart joining the rotation. Sheppard should remain part of the mix after averaging 13.5 points in 26.2 minutes last season, but Amen Thompson also handles the ball and can initiate offense. Sheppard also averaged 1.5 steals per game, which gives him a useful fantasy floor even if his playmaking role stays limited.

What to watch for: Whether Sheppard runs the offense when VanVleet sits or spends most of his time off the ball. If Houston gives him regular creation work and closing minutes, he becomes much more appealing in standard leagues. If not, his value will depend more heavily on threes and steals.

Orlando Magic backcourt: Jalen Suggs, Anthony Black, Jase Richardson

articles.headline: 2027 NFL draft rankings: Jordan Reid's top 50 prospects, scouting reports
articles.description: Jordan Reid unveils his debut rankings for the 2027 NFL draft class with 50 players -- including six quarterbacks and an elite wide receiver prospect.
articles.body:
With the calendar turning to October, it's time to start stacking the top prospects in the 2027 NFL draft class, which begins on April 29 in Washington, D.C. I've been watching and evaluating these players for a couple of years in some instances, and these rankings are a compilation of my scouting (both on film and in person) and conversations I've been having with scouts and evaluators around the NFL.

We're going to start these rankings with 50 players, with scouting reports on the top 25, but this list will expand as the draft gets closer and closer. And these rankings will evolve -- some players will shoot up boards, others will fall and still more will ultimately return to school for another year. But this is how I currently see things in the 2027 class.

Let's get to it, starting with arguably the best wide receiver prospect of the past 15-20 years. (And the top names at every position are listed at the bottom.)

Jump to:

Rankings by position

1. Jeremiah Smith, WR, Ohio State

Height: 6-4 | Weight: 222

Smith could have All-Pro potential early in his NFL career as a true No. 1 receiver. He immediately changes the offensive outlook for the team that adds him. He is sure-handed and can glide past defenders with ease. And he's equally as capable of winning with strength at the catch point. Smith's change of direction in routes needs to become sharper, as he can take too many choppy steps when working back toward passers. But he is tough to stop when allowed to attack defenses vertically.

Stats through Oct. 1: 33 receptions for 617 receiving yards (18.7 yards per reception) and seven touchdowns

2. Leonard Moore, CB, Notre Dame

Height: 6-2 | Weight: 197

With excellent length, speed and technique, Moore is the prototypical cornerback prospect. His length and physicality allow him to excel when getting hands on receivers in press man coverage. He also has the awareness to identify and defend route concepts in zone coverage. Moore has the ball skills to match receivers, routinely tracking and attacking the ball out of the air. But he needs to improve his discipline and hand timing at the top of routes.

Stats through Oct. 1: Seven tackles, two passes defensed, 0% completion percentage allowed

3. Colin Simmons, Edge, Texas

Height: 6-3 | Weight: 246

Simmons is an energetic and high-effort pass rusher, with a quick first step to explode past blockers. He has a nifty combination of hesitation moves and shoulder fakes. But he still needs to develop consistent counter moves, as he can get stuck if his initial move isn't effective. Simmons is a powerful run defender, using a strong base and hands to keep his frame clean when setting the edge.

Stats through Oct. 1: 13 tackles, 7.5 sacks, nine tackles for loss, one forced fumble, one fumble recovery

4. Will Echoles, DT, Ole Miss

Height: 6-3 | Weight: 315

An explosive 3-technique, Echoles is one of the most versatile and well-conditioned interior defenders in the country. He has energetic hands

articles.headline: Roberto De Zerbi receives backing of Tottenham's chief executive
articles.description: Chief executive Vinai Venkatesham has offered his backing to Roberto De Zerbi after Tottenham's poor start to the new campaign.
articles.body:
Tottenham chief executive Vinai Venkatesham has offered his backing to Roberto De Zerbi after Tottenham's poor start to the new campaign.

Spurs are bottom of the Premier League and winless after five fixtures despite a summer of lavish spending where more than £380 million ($501m) was committed on new players.

However, Venkatesham pointed to the "underlying performances" with Tottenham able to create plenty of good openings without scoring in matches against Newcastle, Nottingham Forest and Everton.

Speaking during last week's first Fan Advisory Board meeting of the season, Venkatesham noted he was "encouraged by aspects of the underlying performances since the opening day defeat [at Brentford]."

The Spurs CEO "acknowledged the disappointment at the current points total even at this early point in the season and recognised the frustration this caused supporters following the previous campaign."

 

Venkatesham was quick to point out his belief in De Zerbi and the revamped playing group after 10 new signings joined along with the departures of experienced players like Guglielmo Vicario, Djed Spence, Cristian Romero, Kevin Danso and João Palhinha.

"The club had made significant changes over the summer, both on and off the pitch, and recognised that these might take time to take full effect," Venkatesham told the meeting.

"[Venkatesham] expressed confidence in Roberto De Zerbi, in the players brought in and in the changes made, noting the considerable work under way behind the scenes."

While Tottenham spent big to secure Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes and Sávio, the club made around £150m ($198m) in departures with highly-rated teenager Luka Vuskovic allowed to join Brighton in a £50m ($66m) deal.

Further significant fees will follow next summer after Radu Dragusin and Danso left with obligations to turn their loans into permanent moves and Vicario and Pape Sarr could also bring in funds given their exits to Juventus included an option to depart permanently.

After Spurs' majority owners the Lewis family injected another £120m ($158m) in capital last month, Venkatesham laid out the financial "constraint" on the north London club.

- Premier League depth charts for most popular teams: Who is key?

- Jan Paul van Hecke returns to Tottenham after suffering foot injury with Netherlands

Venkatesham told the meeting: "The club needed to improve as a seller of players, having achieved limited returns in previous years and doing so is important in modern football for compliance with financial regulations."

He continued: "Financial regulations represented a genuine constraint. The club had not recorded a profit since 2019 and its costs were rising through investment in the men's team in wages and transfer fees.

"Successive 17th-placed finishes and the absence of European revenue this season had also affected the club's revenue position."

It was confirmed "significant changes" had been made to Spurs' performance team across medical, physical prep

articles.headline: Fantasy football: Six players to trade for, two to pick up
articles.description: Matt Bowen discusses ascending players who are intriguing trade or pickup options.
articles.body:
Over the first couple of weeks in this space, we focused on the players failing to meet preseason expectations. Justin Herbert, Colston Loveland and Marvin Harrison Jr. have had rough starts that forced managers to make tough decisions for their lineups.

So, I wanted to write something more positive heading into Week 4, looking at the fantasy targets who are playing at a higher level or showing flashes that point to potential upside. Volume receivers in the pass game, a quarterback throwing with consistency from the pocket in a big-time offense and the rookies jumping off the tape.

Below are eight ascending players to consider trading for or adding to your rosters.

Six players to trade for

DJ Moore, WR, Buffalo Bills

This is an ideal time to get Moore in a trade. He had an early shoulder injury in the Week 2 game versus Detroit that wiped out his day (minus-0.1 points), and he followed that up with six receptions for 67 yards (12.3 points) in the Bills' Week 3 win over the Chargers. But if we look deeper at the numbers, plus his route deployment, Moore has excellent value in an explosive Bills offense.

In Weeks 1 and 3, when Moore played a full game, he saw at least eight targets, with a target share of 33.5%, a number that jumps to 50% on third downs. Moore is also the vertical option for Josh Allen, as he's already seen six targets of 15 or more air yards. Plus, the Bills can scheme for Moore as a motion/movement player, getting him free access off the ball to beat man coverage or targeting him on boot and screen concepts.

The Bills are going to score points at a high rate, and Moore is the top target in this offense. Don't be surprised if Moore produces some WR1 weeks.

Jared Goff, QB, Detroit Lions

Goff is scoring 21.2 fantasy PPG despite very limited rushing totals (15 yards) because he's one of the league's best pocket throwers. Goff has completed 70.6% of passes this season, and he has at least two touchdown throws in all three games. He's a rhythm passer in an offense scoring 31.0 PPG (third most), and that Detroit defense is really struggling to find an identity (allowing a league-worst 31.7 PPG), which can lead to more shootouts for Goff.

Now, can you get Goff in a trade? The arrow is pointing up, but let's look for managers in 10- or 12-team leagues who drafted Goff as their QB2. Make a move now because Goff can be used as a matchup-based starter, and his upcoming schedule (@CAR, @ARI, BYE, GB) looks really good. He's going to get you 16 to 18 points a week, and we can win with that.

Parker Washington, WR, Jacksonville Jaguars

The value is up for Washington, as he's scoring 16.4 fantasy PPG, while seeing a target share of 30.3%. He has caught a touchdown in two of three games played. Maybe you have to offer more than you would have at the beginning of the season. I get it. articles.headline: Are we seeing more NFL quarterback injuries than normal this season?
articles.description: There have been eight QB injuries through three weeks of the NFL season, up a little bit from recent years. Is it a trend or just an outlier -- and is there a clear reason?
articles.body:
It happened again. Just when it looked like we might get through a Sunday without an NFL quarterback getting injured for the first time in 2026, Tampa Bay's Baker Mayfield went down in pain against the Vikings. On a day when Mayfield was sacked six times and knocked down on four more dropbacks, a glancing blow proved to be the most painful hit, as the Bucs starter suffered a dislocated thumb while trying to get the ball out on fourth down. The injury is expected to cost Mayfield about three weeks, which only makes life harder for the winless Buccaneers, who will now turn to Jalon Daniels in the meantime.

Then, on "Monday Night Football," both teams dealt with quarterback injuries. The Bears started Case Keenum after Caleb Williams injured his hamstring and Tyson Bagent spent most of the week in concussion protocol. The Eagles briefly lost Jalen Hurts to a concussion check of his own, and while he quickly returned to the game, he was out of the lineup just long enough for Andy Dalton to throw a critical interception in the end zone to end an Eagles drive.

Depending on who you define as each team's primary option, Mayfield was somewhere between the sixth, seventh, eighth or even ninth starting quarterback to go down so far this season. The Bears likely would have started Bagent if not for the time in concussion protocol, but he didn't actually miss any action. Hurts was back quickly, as Dalton threw only one pass. You could argue that the Falcons would have started either Tua Tagovailoa or Michael Penix Jr. in Week 1; both were injured, leaving them to start Cooper Rush instead.

The NFL made it exactly zero drives without a starting quarterback going down this season, as Sam Darnold suffered a glute injury before the end of Seattle's opening possession in the season opener. He's already back after missing a couple of weeks, as is Kyler Murray, who left quickly in Week 1 because of a concussion.

Subscribe: 'The Bill Barnwell Show'

The news was good on Jayden Daniels (elbow) and Williams, who luckily avoided long-term injuries. Giants fans were less fortunate, as early suggestions that Jaxson Dart would be OK eventually turned more ominous. Dart underwent knee surgery to end his season last week. He's currently the only starting quarterback lost for the year.

So, to recap: Seven quarterbacks have been forced out of games by injuries through the first three weeks of the NFL season. Is that a lot? Is it a problem that's getting worse? Are QBs getting hit more often? Are we seeing more backup quarterbacks than ever before? Should teams be investing more in those QB2s as a result? These are all legitimate questions to ask. So, I actually did the research this week to try to figure out how often quarterbacks get hurt early in the season.

articles.headline: Packers' O-line leaves Jordan Love under constant pressure
articles.description: The Packers have allowed more "quick pressures" against Love than any team in the NFL -- and it's not close.
articles.headlineJa: パッカーズのOラインがジョーダン・ラブを常にプレッシャーに晒す
articles.descriptionJa: パッカーズがラブに対して許した「クイックプレッシャー」の数はNFLのどのチームよりも多く、圧倒的な差となっている。
articles.body:
GREEN BAY, Wis. -- When Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love said after last week's 35-14 loss to the Atlanta Falcons that he needs to make quicker decisions, the next question should have been: How much quicker can he possibly make them given the light speed with which opposing pass rushers have been in his face?

According to Next Gen Stats, the Packers have allowed the most "quick pressures" -- defined as pressure on the quarterback in less than 2.5 seconds -- in the NFL, and it's not close. Love has been quick pressured 37 times in three games. No other team has allowed more than 28.

In last Thursday's loss, the Falcons recorded 15 quick pressures, second most in a game this season. The most was the 17 the Packers allowed to the Vikings in Week 1.

"Obviously you always need time," Love said Wednesday. "The more time you have, the better you're able to pick apart the defense and find those completions. That's with anything, you always want time. Obviously there's times you might not have time, you've got to find those answers.

"That's an area that we've got to improve on, in pass [protection], making sure we're going to the right people and sustaining blocks for as long as we can, give me some time to pick the defense apart and obviously something that we need to improve on."

At some point, the concern is the impact it will have on Love -- both from a fundamental standpoint and when it comes to his health -- if it hasn't already. The concern is that a quarterback who has been hit so many times can start to feel pressure even when it's not there, or as coaches and scouts call it, "seeing ghosts."

"There's definitely some plays, especially later in the [Falcons] game, where we talked about my feet are just getting a little bit off and that definitely is some of the pressure being a factor in that," Love said. "In that scenario, I've just got to be better right there.

"I can improve my game to make sure I'm staying on schedule, trusting my feet, reading with my feet, and it's going to help me be as accurate as possible. But I think it's a natural reaction sometimes as a quarterback, you might feel sped up. I've got to fight that urge and trust my feet and still be great in the pocket."

While Love has thrown for the fourth-most yards (844) through three games and has six touchdown passes against two interceptions, the problem is that he has a 1.7 QBR when pressured. That's the second lowest in the NFL ahead of Denver's Bo Nix (1.1). Love has a 31% completion rate, no touchdowns and both of his interceptions when pressured.

Teams might even try to send more rushers after Love. He ranks only 10th in pressure percentage this season, according to ESPN tracking, taking pressure on 38% of his dropbacks. However, that could be in part because he's averaging 2.49 seconds per pass, the quickest in the league according to Next Gen Stats. He averaged 2.84 seconds in his first three seasons as a starter.

articles.headline: Browns' QB situation takes a turn as Deshaun Watson finds his footing
articles.description: Cleveland's 2-1 start and the QB's late-game performances have helped to shift the conversation around the future of the position.
articles.headlineJa: デショーン・ワトソンが復調の兆しを見せ、ブラウンズのQB事情に変化
articles.descriptionJa: クリーブランドの2勝1敗のスタートと、試合終盤における同QBの活躍により、このポジションの将来を巡る議論の流れが変わりつつある。
articles.body:
DESHAUN WATSON JOGGED toward the tunnel leading to the Cleveland Browns' locker room at Huntington Bank Field surrounded by cheers last Sunday -- a stark contrast to the loud boos he received the last time he played in front of the hometown fans.

Waiting outside the locker room for the Browns' starting quarterback was general manager Andrew Berry, who smiled broadly. The two shared a handshake and hug. With Berry's arm around Watson's shoulder, they turned, ready to celebrate with the team.

The sequence leading to that scene and the change in reception from fans was a game-winning touchdown drive to defeat the Carolina Panthers 21-18 in Week 3. The win marked Watson's second fourth-quarter comeback in as many weeks, which seemed implausible after a late August preseason game, when Watson struggled in the second half, was loudly booed, and later lashed out at fans in the postgame news conference.

That preseason discontent seemed like the final chapter for a player who received a five-year, fully guaranteed $230 million contract in March 2022 but was crumbling under high expectations in Cleveland. Through four seasons, 19 mostly underwhelming performances were sandwiched between an 11-game suspension after more than two dozen women accused him of sexual assault and inappropriate conduct during massage sessions, and multiple significant injuries since Cleveland traded three first-round picks to the Houston Texans for Watson.

Entering the 2026 season, the consensus view among Cleveland spectators was that the Browns might finally part ways with Watson at the end of the regular season, taking an exorbitant $86 million dead cap hit while possibly turning to the 2027 NFL draft -- with the Browns holding two first-round picks -- to solve the franchise's perpetual quarterback conundrum. Such a conclusion would render playing Watson pointless.

Instead, Watson emerged as the starter following a monthslong competition. His late-game performances and the Browns' 2-1 start have added another wrinkle to the NFL's most confounding quarterback dynamic: Cleveland enters its "Thursday Night Football" home game against the Pittsburgh Steelers (8:15 p.m. ET, Prime Video) with first place in the AFC North on the line.

"[Watson] is playing pretty well. At least give him enough of a sample size to see what he can do," an NFC executive told ESPN.

While team sources indicated that Watson's performance through three games hasn't convinced the Browns to consider Watson the long-term answer, Cleveland's surprising start has shifted the conversation inside the building to whether the 31-year-old passer and the Browns can build short-term momentum.

"I feel like I have a lot of football left in my game, in my career, and that's how I approach the game," Watson said last week. "That's how I approach my preparation on and off the field. I feel like I'm 10 years in, but still got a lot of football to play, definitely for myself."

articles.headline: Clásico match ball for Barcelona vs. Real Madrid LaLiga clashes unveiled
articles.description: Whenever LaLiga rivals Barcelona and Real Madrid clash, the world watches. So it's only fitting that El Clásico gets its own bespoke match ball.
articles.headlineJa: バルセロナ対レアル・マドリードのラ・リーガ「クラシコ」専用試合球が公開
articles.descriptionJa: ラ・リーガのライバルであるバルセロナとレアル・マドリードが激突する時、世界中が注目する。それだけに、エル・クラシコのために専用の特別試合球が用意されるのはまさに相応しい。
articles.body:
Whenever bitter LaLiga rivals Barcelona and Real Madrid clash in El Clásico, it's a match that the world watches.

The next time that happens will be later this month, when Barça host Madrid at Camp Nou on Sunday, Oct. 25 (stream the match LIVE on ESPN+ in the U.S.).

But, just to add a little extra luster to a fixture that is already positively dripping in it, Puma has revealed their new bespoke match ball that is to be used for the two league meetings between Spanish football's twin heavyweights.

For the second year running, Puma has designed a special "ELCLASICO" ball which combines eye-catching colours and retro-tinged graphics to herald the monumental contest.

White with flashes of gold and black, the new ball is a custom variant of the official LaLiga 2026-27 match ball -- the Stellar Nitro Ultimate. It is an updated version of the inaugural Puma ELCLASICO model, a ball which was first used in October 2025.

On that day, Madrid beat Barça 2-1 at the Bernabéu thanks to goals from Kylian Mbappé and Jude Bellingham. However, Madrid coach Xabi Alonso was fired three months later, and Barça had the last laugh as they retained their LaLiga crown and helped consign their rivals to a second consecutive season without a major trophy.

Barça have made a flying start to the 2026-27 season, winning all seven of their league games so far and scoring 31 along the way. Madrid are six points and three points below them in the table, so they will already be facing a crucial point in their season when they travel to Catalonia in just over three weeks' time.

articles.headline: Premier League 'dragged through the mud' by Man City case - Gary Neville
articles.description: The Premier League has been "dragged through the mud" by the Manchester City guilty verdict, Gary Neville has said.
articles.headlineJa: プレミアリーグはマンCの件で「泥を塗られた」― ゲイリー・ネヴィル
articles.descriptionJa: ゲイリー・ネヴィル氏は、マンチェスター・シティの有罪判決によってプレミアリーグが「泥を塗られた」と述べた。
articles.body:
The Premier League has been "dragged through the mud" by the Manchester City guilty verdict, Gary Neville has said.

An independent commission found City guilty on all charges related to breaching Premier League financial rules, concluding they "clearly intended to circumvent" the regulations over a period of nine seasons, primarily by disguising owner funding as sponsorship revenue.

Former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher has called on the club's owner Sheikh Mansour to sell up, while former Manchester United full-back Neville believes the reputation of the whole league has been affected.

"To listen to this, it is chilling," he said on the Stick To Football podcast.

 

"We always think that we've got an enormous integrity, the Premier League, that we are the sort of league that sets the standard, and that it's other leagues that have got corruption, fraud, doping scandals, match-fixing, referee scandals.

"This is now coming to our country. This is now coming to our league. This is the greatest export that we have in our country. At the moment we're being dragged through the mud."

City were found to have inflated revenue and hid costs to the tune of more than £900 million ($1.1 billion) across the nine-season period, and in doing so avoided breaching Premier League and UEFA spending limits.

- Man City vs. Premier League: 115 financial charges explained

- Man City should be stripped of titles - Jamie Carragher

- Does Man City's guilty verdict impact Pep Guardiola's legacy as an all-time coaching great?

They have indicated their intention to appeal against the commission's decision, saying it "contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe."

City said "a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all [the club's] positions."

Neville described the "irrefutable evidence" remark as "bizarre," adding: "It was a bit Trump-esque, wasn't it?"
